summary: Handler.ts is the entire yeet execution engine: it defines the public run option/result schemas, Turbo/gh JSON schemas and decoders, git/gh/turbo subprocess wrappers, publish-scope safety (intent, stash, base freshness), durable proof state and locking, issue-artifact writing, and the per-mode orchestration (runYeet + repair/verify/publish/monitor/closeout/status/pre-push-hook) in one 2897-line module.

concerns.name: Turbo query schemas + snapshot collection
concerns.description: Schema classes for `turbo query affected`/`turbo query ls` JSON, their decoders, subprocess invocation, and mapping into TurboPlanSnapshot/TurboPlanTask. Includes the O(n) balanced-brace JSON extractor for mixed subprocess output.

concerns.name: Public command data schemas
concerns.description: The facade-exported option/result models plus the publish-intent value object, with large @example doc blocks. These are the only Handler symbols re-exported by commands/Yeet/index.ts.

concerns.name: Pure publish-scope path domain logic
concerns.description: Pure functions over git path lists: NUL-output parsing, pre-push SHA extraction/mismatch, intent-diff computations, partial-stage/overlap detection, path summarization, and refname safety, each with a *ForTesting alias.

concerns.name: Git/gh subprocess wrappers
concerns.description: Effectful wrappers over runRepoCommandCapture for git and gh: output capture with exit/truncation checks, path-list collection, base-ref refresh with injection guarding, upstream inspection, lockfile change detection.

concerns.name: GitHub PR lifecycle
concerns.description: gh pr view/create integration: PR metadata schema, open-PR discovery, PR body rendering from commit log + lane summary, idempotent PR creation, and monitor PR validation.

concerns.name: Flag-combination guard validation
concerns.description: A long conditional wall validating mode/flag combinations (--fast, --start-pr-early, --push-only, --staged-only, --amend, --no-edit, --pr) plus commit-message presence and commitlint execution.

concerns.name: Publish intent + staged-only stash safety
concerns.description: Collecting the reviewed publish intent, re-validating it after quality lanes, restaging, post-commit worktree drift checks, and the marked-stash park/restore for --staged-only, all failing through packet-writing errors.

concerns.name: Durable proof state, fingerprint, and lock
concerns.description: SHA-256 diff fingerprinting via git diff --output into guarded artifact paths, YeetRunState/YeetLaneProofState/YeetProofLockState schemas, exclusive O_EXCL lock claim with stale-pid disposition, and verified-state write/load/reuse assertions.

concerns.name: Artifact + issue packet writing
concerns.description: Filesystem helpers (mkdir+write), JSON rendering, quality-issue index + per-package markdown packet emission, step log paths, and failure paths that write packets before raising YeetCommandError.

concerns.name: Mode orchestration and entrypoint
concerns.description: Phase execution over the plan (prepare/feedback/commit/full/publish/monitor), the seven YeetRunMode branches, verdict writing on success/failure, plan rendering, context hydration, and the exported runYeet entrypoint.

proposedSplit.contents: YeetRunOptions, YeetRunResult, YeetPublishIntent, and defaultYeetRunOptions (the constructor-with-defaults test helper belongs beside the schema). index.ts re-exports YeetRunOptions/YeetRunResult from here instead of internal/Handler.js.

TurboQuery* schema classes and decoders, runTurboQueryJson, collectTurboVersion, collectAffectedFeedbackTasks, collectTurboPlanSnapshot, turboPlanTasksFromQueryDocuments, shouldCollectAffectedFeedbackTasks, plus balancedTopLevelObjectSpans/isEscapedQuote/jsonObjectTextFromMixedOutput and the jsonObjectTextFromMixedOutputForTesting/decodeTurboPlanTasksFromQueryJsonForTesting aliases.

runGitOutput, runGitPathList, collectStagedPublishPaths/collectUnstagedTrackedPaths/collectUntrackedPaths, currentCommitSha, refreshBaseRef, originBranchFromBase, isSafeOriginBranch, safeOriginBranchFromBaseForTesting, collectCurrentUpstreamBranch, lockfileChangedSinceBase, commandFailure, optionFromNonEmpty.

Pure path domain logic (sortedUniquePaths, gitPathListFromNulOutput, prePush*, publishPathsOutsideIntent, publishRestagePaths, partiallyStagedPaths, overlappingBasePaths, summarizePublishPaths, publishUpstreamMismatchWarning) plus the effectful intent safety chain: failPublishScopeWithPacket, collectPublishIntent, validatePublishIntentStillSafe, stageReviewedPublishIntent, validatePostCommitProofDidNotChangeWorktree, assessBaseFreshness, enforceBaseFreshness, stash park/restore, and all their *ForTesting aliases.

YeetRunState, YeetLaneProofState, YeetProofLockState schemas; collectDiffFingerprint/collectGitDiffBytes/hashText/laneProofStateForStep/proofCommandForSteps; lock machinery (isPidAlive, proofLockDisposition, tryClaimProofLockExclusive, acquireFullProofLock, releaseProofLock, proofLockPathForContext); writeVerifiedState, loadVerifiedState, legacyRunStatePathForContext, assertReusableVerifiedState; ForTesting aliases (collectDiffFingerprintForTesting, proofLockDispositionForTesting, loadVerifiedStateForTesting, YeetProofLockStateForTesting).
GhPullRequestView schema + decoder, runGhPullRequestView, findOpenPullRequest, buildPrBody, recordPrCreateLane, ensurePullRequest, validateOpenPullRequest.
validateMonitorGuards (the flag-combination wall), validateMonitorBranch, blockedMonitorBranches, shouldMonitorChecks, validateRequiredMessage, validateCommitMessage, commitMessagePathForContext.

writeTextFile, renderJson/encodeJson, writeIssueArtifacts, issuesFromResults, failWithIssueArtifacts, executeStepWithArtifacts, rawOutputPathForStep, publishResult, emptyPlanResult. Sits above ArtifactPaths.ts and below every mode module; breaks the current failPublishScopeWithPacket -> writeIssueArtifacts forward reference.

Remains the orchestrator (~600-700 LOC): runYeet, hydrateYeetRunContext, runPlanExecution, runPhase/runProofPhase/runRequiredPhase, runVerifyMode/runPublishMode/runMonitorMode/runStatusMode/runCloseoutMode/runPrePushHookMode/readPrePushHookStdin, shouldSkipCommitForReusablePublish(+ForTesting), writeRunVerdict, YeetVerdictExtras, renderPlan, printOperatorStatusSummary, buildYeetRunPlanForTesting.

sharedCandidates.description: Generic capture-with-exit/truncation-check wrappers over runRepoCommandCapture for git. Worktree.command.ts already hand-rolls its own runGitCapture (line 389); belongs in src/internal/repo-run alongside runRepoCommandCapture.
Provider-agnostic extraction of the last decodable top-level JSON object from noisy subprocess output (the O(n) hang-fix scanner). Nothing about it is yeet- or turbo-specific.

mkdir-recursive + writeFileString with a tagged error; the same pattern is re-implemented in several command internals that emit artifacts. Only the error constructor is command-specific, so a shared version would take an error mapper.

Generic O_EXCL file-lock claim with stale-owner-pid detection and replace/refuse disposition. Useful for any long-running CLI lane that must serialize (only the YeetProofLockState payload is command-specific).

Git refname safety validation (rejects option-like, refspec, and glob metacharacters) complementing guardLiteralArg in @beep/repo-utils; any command that fetches or checks out user-supplied refs needs it.
gh pr view JSON schema and open-PR discovery; Closeout.ts in the same group and any CI-facing command duplicate gh JSON plumbing.
Pure NUL-delimited git output parsing and dedupe/sort; generic to any git path listing.
trim + non-empty -> Option<string>; a two-line generic helper that likely already has (or deserves) a home in @beep/repo-utils or a shared string module rather than per-command copies.

risks: Facade breakage: commands/Yeet/index.ts re-exports YeetRunOptions/YeetRunResult from ./internal/Handler.js and Yeet.command.ts deep-imports runYeet + YeetRunOptions from internal/Handler.js; both import sites must be updated in the same change.

Test-kit star-export collisions: src/test/Yeet.test-kit.ts does `export * from "../commands/Yeet/internal/Handler.js"` and test/yeet.test.ts imports ~40 symbols (many *ForTesting aliases) through @beep/repo-cli/test/Yeet; every new internal module must be added to the test-kit, and if Handler re-exports moved symbols while the test-kit also stars the new module, duplicate-export errors or ambiguity will surface.

Schema identity churn: schema classes use $I = $RepoCliId.create("commands/Yeet/internal/Handler"), so moving YeetRunOptions/YeetRunState/Turbo* classes changes their identifier strings and the generated, tracked P3 schema catalog must be regenerated (structural JSON decode of persisted state.json/quality-lock is unaffected, but catalog diffs will gate).

Effect ordering/state coupling: runProofPhase wraps runPhase in acquireUseRelease of the proof lock, stash restore rides Effect.ensuring around runPostCommitPhases, and the recorder/extras Refs are threaded through every phase — the split must preserve exact effect ordering (park stash BEFORE commit, validate intent twice around git add, verdict write in tapError/tap) or publish safety guarantees silently weaken.

Docgen gates: moved exports carry @example blocks that import from @beep/repo-cli/commands/Yeet and @beep/repo-cli/test/Yeet; examples must stay compilable from the new files and every new file needs @packageDocumentation/@since to pass `bun run docgen`.

Layering to avoid cycles: failPublishScopeWithPacket (PublishScope) needs writeIssueArtifacts (IssueArtifacts) which needs QualityIssueIndex/PacketRenderer; GitExec must not import PublishScope; enforce GitExec -> PublishScope -> IssueArtifacts -> Handler direction or the split reintroduces the current forward-reference tangle as import cycles.

summary: Implements the `yeet closeout` mode end-to-end: it shells out to `gh` (pr/repo view, paginated GraphQL queries, thread reply/resolve mutations), decodes the GitHub payloads into ~30 schema classes, derives Greptile/bot review signal, computes closeout gate states and QualityIssues, optionally performs explicit review-thread write actions, and emits the durable PrCloseoutReport consumed by Handler.ts and Status.ts.

concerns.name: GitHub GraphQL response schemas
concerns.description: Approximately 25 S.Class wrappers mirroring gh GraphQL payload shapes (actor, page info, comments, review threads, reviews, plus per-query Repository/Data/Document envelope triples). Pure data modeling with zero behavior.

concerns.name: Closeout domain schemas (public)
concerns.description: The command's own data models: gate options, Greptile summary, durable gate state (LiteralKit name/status), write action, and the versioned PrCloseoutReport persisted as a run artifact and re-decoded by Status.ts.

concerns.name: GraphQL query documents + JSON decoders
concerns.description: Three inline GraphQL page query strings, two thread mutations, and five S.decodeUnknownEffect(S.fromJsonString(...)) decoders binding queries to schemas.

concerns.name: gh process execution wrapper
concerns.description: ghOutput runs runRepoCommandCapture("gh", ...) and maps nonzero exit / truncated capture into YeetCommandError. Single generic helper reused by every gh call in the file.

concerns.name: Pure Greptile/bot signal parsing
concerns.description: Regex-based parsing of Greptile score/issue-count from comment bodies, bot-token matching, and fail-closed issue-count inference; entirely pure with two ForTesting exports that wrap internals.

concerns.name: Gate-state and QualityIssue derivation
concerns.description: Pure functions building QualityIssue records (via QualityIssueIndex constructors) and the five PrCloseoutGateState values (review-threads, greptile, coderabbit, chatgpt, hosted-checks) from options + parsed signal.

concerns.name: GraphQL pagination collectors (effectful)
concerns.description: Cursor plumbing (nextCursor, cursorArgs) and three while-loop page collectors plus collectPrCloseoutPayload composing gh pr view + repo view + all three collectors; logs warnings on >100 nested comments.

concerns.name: Write-action planning (pure) and execution
concerns.description: closeoutWritePlan validates --reply-thread/--reply-body/--resolve-threads flags against known thread ids into typed intents (pure); performCloseoutWriteActions executes them serially via gh GraphQL mutations.

concerns.name: Closeout orchestrator
concerns.description: runPrCloseout wires everything: fetch payload, optionally plan+perform writes then refetch (mutable let rebinding), derive bot comments/signal/issues/gate states, optionally post the Greptile retrigger comment, and construct PrCloseoutReport.

proposedSplit.contents: All ~25 Gh* GraphQL response S.Class wrappers (GhActor through GhReviewsDocument, GhPrView, GhRepoView) plus the five decodeGh* decoders and the three page query strings they decode. Self-contained cluster with no dependency on the rest of the file.

Public domain models: PrCloseoutOptions, GreptileSummary, PrCloseoutGateName/PrCloseoutGateStatus LiteralKits, PrCloseoutGateState, PrCloseoutWriteAction, PrCloseoutReport (depends only on QualityIssueIndex and Gh.schemas is not needed).

Pure signal parsing: normalizedTokens, authorLogin, textMatchesAnyToken, isBotComment, isGreptileComment, score/issue-count regexes and parsers, latestGreptileSummary(+ForTesting), bot/greptile thread counters, hasGreptileEvidence, inferGreptileIssueCount(+ForTesting).

Pure gate/issue derivation: issueRouting, closeoutIssue, reviewThreadIssue, greptileIssueLimitExceeded(+ForTesting), gateIssues, greptileGateState, threadBotGateState, closeoutGateStates(+ForTesting).

Effectful gh execution: ghOutput, cursorArgs, nextCursor, closedPageInfo, ghGraphqlPage, the three collect*Pages loops, collectPrCloseoutPayload, and performCloseoutWriteActions with the two mutation constants.
Pure write planning: CloseoutWriteIntent type, caseSensitiveTokens, CLOSEOUT_REPLY_BODY_MAX_CHARS, closeoutWritePlan(+ForTesting) flag validation against known thread ids.

Shrinks to the runPrCloseout orchestrator, GREPTILE_RETRIGGER_COMMENT(+ForTesting), and a re-export barrel of the public/ForTesting symbols so Handler.ts, Status.ts, and src/test/Yeet.test-kit.ts keep working unchanged.

sharedCandidates.description: Generic 'run gh, map nonzero exit and truncated capture to YeetCommandError' wrapper. Handler.ts (runGhPullRequestView, findOpenPullRequest ~line 623+) and Status.ts (collectRemoteChecks/collectRemoteStatus ~line 382+) hand-roll the identical exitCode/truncated dance; a parameterized runGhCapture in src/internal/repo-run/ would collapse all three (error type would need to be caller-supplied or a shared repo-run error).
Generic GitHub GraphQL cursor-pagination machinery, not closeout-specific. Any future gh GraphQL consumer (Research repo cards, AIMetrics PR data) needs exactly this loop.

Generic GitHub payload shapes; GhPrView (number,headRefName,state,url,headRefOid,isDraft) is a superset duplicate of Handler.ts's GhPullRequestView (number,headRefName,state) decoded from the same gh pr view command. A shared internal/github schema module would deduplicate.
Comma-separated CLI flag tokenizers (trim, drop empties, optional lowercase); generic flag-parsing utilities useful to any command group accepting CSV flags.

risks: src/test/Yeet.test-kit.ts does `export * from "../commands/Yeet/internal/Closeout.js"` and test/yeet.test.ts consumes PrCloseoutOptions, PrCloseoutReport, GreptileSummary, and five *ForTesting helpers through it — the barrel at internal/Closeout.ts must keep re-exporting everything (or test-kit must re-export each new module, risking export* name collisions).

$I keys embed the module path (`$RepoCliId.create("commands/Yeet/internal/Closeout")`); moving S.Class declarations to new files changes schema identifiers/annotations unless each new file keeps or deliberately re-derives its $I path — affects docgen output and any identifier-sensitive tooling (PrCloseoutReport JSON round-trip via Status.ts decodePrCloseoutReport is structural and safe, but keep the "yeet-pr-closeout/v1" literal).
Deep imports to update: Handler.ts imports { PrCloseoutOptions, runPrCloseout } and Status.ts imports { PrCloseoutReport } from ./Closeout.js — keep them working via the barrel or rewrite both.

runPrCloseout has strict ordering with mutable rebinding: collect payload -> plan/perform writes -> re-collect payload -> derive gates from refreshed data -> post Greptile retrigger comment LAST (so the retrigger comment never feeds the same run's gate evaluation); a split must not let the orchestrator compute gates from the pre-write payload or reorder the retrigger.

JSDoc @example blocks reference facade paths ("@beep/repo-cli/commands/Yeet", "@beep/repo-cli/test/Yeet") that docgen compiles; note PrCloseoutGateState's example imports from commands/Yeet whose index.ts does not actually export it — a pre-existing inconsistency a refactor could trip over.

test/schema-first.test.ts is already modified in the working tree and lints schema layout; distributing S.Class declarations across new files may change its counts/expectations and the crispening ratchet.

summary: Schema-first domain model plus the entire normalization pipeline for yeet quality findings: it defines the QualityIssue* schema family, parses raw failed-step output (TS diagnostics, schema-first JSON lines, known sub-lane heuristics) into QualityIssue values, resolves package/turbo attribution from RepoRunContext, and aggregates issues into a deterministic QualityIssueIndex.

concerns.name: Public quality-issue schema models
concerns.description: LiteralKit domains and S.Class models that form the yeet packet wire format; all eight are re-exported through commands/Yeet/index.ts.

concerns.name: Schema-first policy wire decoding
concerns.description: Private duplicate of the '[schema-first:issue] ' JSON-line protocol emitted by Lint/SchemaFirst.ts, decoded via S.fromJsonString. The same schema+prefix is independently re-declared in AgentEffectiveness/internal/EvalScorer.ts (SchemaFirstPolicyIssue).

concerns.name: Raw-output text normalization
concerns.description: Generic subprocess-output text utilities: ANSI stripping, line splitting/trimming, excerpt truncation. Nothing yeet-specific; bin-main.ts hand-rolls its own nonEmptyLines.

concerns.name: Category classification and specialist routing heuristics
concerns.description: Step-label to category mapping, the knownSubLaneHints needle table with remediation text, failure-window scanning over output tails, and category-to-skill routing. Pure functions plus one export consumed by Verdict.ts and tests.

concerns.name: Turbo/workspace context resolution
concerns.description: Pure lookups over RepoRunContext/TurboPlanTask: workspace package catalog merge, file-to-package attribution, package-path and turbo-task resolution, --filter= arg extraction. Only depends on internal/repo-run types, not on QualityIssue.

concerns.name: Issue construction and step-result parsing
concerns.description: Stable issue-id derivation, the large issueBase spread (turbo hash/cache attribution via optionalProp), TS-diagnostic line parsing, fallback raw issues per filtered package, and the dual-arity qualityIssuesFromStepResult entry point.

concerns.name: Index aggregation and deterministic grouping
concerns.description: Order instances, the NUL-separated packageKey, per-package report construction, and buildQualityIssueIndex producing the sorted, deduped index consumed by Handler and FallowFeedback.

proposedSplit.contents: The eight public schema symbols (QualityIssueCategory/Severity/Confidence/Attribution, QualityIssueRouting, QualityIssue, PackageQualityReport, QualityIssueIndex) plus their LiteralKit domains. index.ts facade re-exports from here instead of the internal file.

categoryForStep, routeForCategory, knownSubLaneHints table, failure-window scanning (outputFailureHintSlices, lineIndicatesFailure, knownSubLaneHintFromText/FromFailureSlices/FromOutput), and the exported knownSubLaneRemediationFromOutput used by Verdict.ts and yeet.test.ts. Depends only on Yeet.schemas.ts and RepoPlanStep.

issueId, issueBase, diagnosticIssueFromLine (tsDiagnosticPattern, severityForLine, lineIndicatesEffectDiagnostic), schemaFirstPolicyIssueFromLine, fallbackIssueFromResult(s), and the dual-arity qualityIssuesFromStepResult. Imports schemas, IssueClassification, workspace resolution, and the shared schema-first wire module.

Retained as the aggregation module: issueOrder, packageReportOrder, packageKey, packageReportForKey, buildQualityIssueIndex. Optionally re-exports the moved symbols one release to soften churn for Handler/FallowFeedback/Closeout/PacketRenderer imports.

Pure RepoRunContext lookups: workspacePackagesForContext, packageNameForFile, packagePathForPackageName, turboTaskForPackageName, turboWorkspacePackageFromTask, filteredPackageNamesForStep, packageNameFromFilterArg, optionalStringFromStep. These operate solely on repo-run types and belong next to them, exported via internal/repo-run/index.ts.

Single source of truth for the '[schema-first:issue] ' prefix and the SchemaFirstPolicyOutput wire class + JSON-line decoder, currently triplicated in Lint/SchemaFirst.ts (emitter, line 451), AgentEffectiveness/internal/EvalScorer.ts (SchemaFirstPolicyIssue, line 306), and this file.
stripAnsi, normalizeOutput, nonEmptyLines, truncateExcerpt (parameterized max chars), optionalNumberFromString. Generic subprocess-output text helpers; bin-main.ts already duplicates nonEmptyLines.

sharedCandidates.description: The '[schema-first:issue] ' JSON-line wire format is declared three times: emitter in Lint/SchemaFirst.ts, this decoder, and AgentEffectiveness/internal/EvalScorer.ts SchemaFirstPolicyIssue. One shared wire schema prevents drift when fields change.
Generic ANSI-stripping and line-normalization for captured subprocess output; src/bin-main.ts:37 hand-rolls its own nonEmptyLines today.
Pure attribution lookups over RepoRunContext and TurboPlanTask with no QualityIssue dependency; any command that runs repo-run plans and needs package attribution can reuse them.
TypeScript 'file:line:col error TSxxxx: message' line parsing is tool-agnostic; the regex-plus-groups extraction (minus QualityIssue wrapping) would serve any group that surfaces tsc/tsgo output.
Tiny Option lifts (parseInt-to-Option, non-empty-string-to-Option) with zero yeet coupling; likely re-derived elsewhere and worth one home in internal/cli.

risks: Public facade breakage: commands/Yeet/index.ts re-exports 8 model symbols from ./internal/QualityIssueIndex.js; moving them to Yeet.schemas.ts must update the facade in the same change or @beep/repo-cli/commands/Yeet consumers break.

Test-kit star export: src/test/Yeet.test-kit.ts does `export * from "../commands/Yeet/internal/QualityIssueIndex.js"` and test/yeet.test.ts imports qualityIssuesFromStepResult, buildQualityIssueIndex, knownSubLaneRemediationFromOutput via @beep/repo-cli/test/Yeet — every new file must be added to the star exports or ~20 test references fail.

Verdict.ts imports with a bare .ts specifier (`from "./QualityIssueIndex.ts"` at line 18) unlike the .js specifiers used by Handler/FallowFeedback/Closeout/PacketRenderer — easy to miss when rewiring imports.

$I identity path: $RepoCliId.create("commands/Yeet/internal/QualityIssueIndex") is baked into every S.Class identifier; moving schemas changes identity keys, which diffs the tracked generated schema catalog (p3) and any serialized annotations — catalog must be regenerated deterministically, though the schemaVersion literal 'yeet-quality-issue-index/v1' itself stays stable.

Docgen gate: every exported symbol carries @example blocks importing from "@beep/repo-cli/commands/Yeet" or "@beep/repo-cli/test/Yeet"; moved symbols must keep those import paths compiling or the docgen-jsdoc-quality lane blocks.

Determinism coupling: issueOrder, packageReportOrder, and the NUL-separated packageKey underpin order-invariance assertions (yeet.test.ts:1270-1291) and stable issue ids consumed by FallowFeedback merge logic — keep them colocated with buildQualityIssueIndex and do not alter matching semantics (lastIndexOf/tail-window logic in knownSubLaneHintFromOutput) while moving.
